summary.text: Matt Slater is a Republican member of the New York State Assembly who has represented District 94, covering parts of Putnam and Westchester counties, since his election in November 2022, and is running for re-election on the Republican and Conservative lines.
He previously served as Yorktown town supervisor.

paragraphs.text: Matt Slater was raised in Yorktown, graduated from Yorktown High School, graduated from St. Anselm College in 2008 and received an MPA from Marist College in 2010.
He served four years as chief of staff to former state Senator Terrence Murphy.
In 2019 he was first elected supervisor of the Town of Yorktown, described in his biography as the town's youngest, and he was re-elected in 2021.
Slater was elected to the Assembly on November 8, 2022.
He serves on the Election Law, Environmental Conservation, Health, Labor, Transportation, and Ways and Means committees.
In 2024 he sponsored the Detective Brian Simonsen Law, which requires cell phone carriers to disable stolen devices once notified of the theft.
According to his biography, he received a Direct Commission as an officer in the Navy Reserves in 2022, and he lives in Yorktown with his wife and two children.
